papers.title_en: Band-Resolved Superconducting Gaps via the Thermal Hall Effect in CeRu2
papers.abstract_en: Standard bulk probes of multiband superconductors cannot assign pairing gaps to specific electron or hole Fermi surfaces. Here we show that thermal Hall transport ($κ_{xy}$), constrained by specific heat and normal-state magnetotransport, resolves this ambiguity in the compensated heavy-fermion superconductor CeRu$_2$. Fixing the gap magnitudes ($Δ_e/k_B\approx 13$K, $Δ_h/k_B\approx 8$K) and band mobilities completely determines the electronic degrees of freedom in $κ_{xx}$ and $κ_{xy}$. A low-field sign reversal in $κ_{xy}$ places the larger gap on the heavy Ce $4f$ electron sheets and the smaller on the hole sheets.

papers.title_en: Integral and higher-genus quantum McKay correspondence in type D
papers.abstract_en: We establish Iritani's integral form of the $\mathbb{C}^\times$-equivariant Crepant Transformation Conjecture (CTC) for the minimal resolution of the surface singularity $\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$, where $\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$ is the binary dihedral group of order $4n$. We then use Givental's quantisation formalism to prove the all-genus full-descendent CTC in that case. As an application, we deduce the Bryan-Cadman-Young degree-zero form of the orbifold Gromov-Witten/Donaldson-Thomas correspondence for the Calabi-Yau 3-orbifold $[\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}] \times \mathbb{C}$.

papers.title_en: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
papers.abstract_en: We present a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), combining a self-contained introduction to its particle-physics foundations and representative benchmark models with an explicit, systematic mapping to simulation inputs and validated numerical implementations in the moving-mesh code AREPO-2. We characterize representative elementary and composite dark-sector models through their particle content, symmetries, interactions, production mechanisms, and constraints. We then establish an explicit mapping from their microscopic properties to the inputs required for structure-formation simulations, including modifications to cosmological initial conditions, internal-state mass splittings and populations, reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, dissipative energy loss, and decay rates and recoil kinematics. Building on the efficient, scalable SIDM infrastructure introduced in our companion work, we implement isotropic and anisotropic self-scattering with constant or velocity-dependent cross sections, multi-state and inelastic reactions, and dissipative scattering, as well as a dedicated DM decay module. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection experiments, thermalization and uniform-box decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. The tests reproduce analytical predictions and published inelastic and dissipative benchmarks, with agreement across numerical schemes. The resulting framework provides a common reference for researchers across disciplines and a practical route from microscopic dark-sector theories to nonlinear astrophysical predictions beyond standard isotropic, elastic SIDM.

papers.title_en: Parafermions in polarized $ν=2/3$ Fractional Quantum (Anomalous) Hall Heterostructures
papers.abstract_en: Motivated by recent experimental signatures of fractional Chern insulators in 2D quantum materials, we investigate the realization of $\mathbb Z_3$ parafermion zero modes (PZMs) on edges of spin-polarized $ν=2/3$ fractional quantum Hall states which are proximitized by superconductors. Unlike the spin-unpolarized Halperin state, the polarized $ν=2/3$ edge contains counterpropagating electron and fractional quasihole modes, giving rise to a plethora of competing tunneling and pairing processes. We focus on the vicinity of the fixed point where these modes reorganize into decoupled charge and neutral sectors, with the neutral sector describing an emergent dipole degree of freedom. Using bosonization and renormalization group analysis, we lay out the parameter space in which the interedge dipole interactions gap the neutral sector to stabilize one dominant tunneling and one dominant pairing channel resulting in a double sine-Gordon model in the charge sector which supports $\mathbb{Z}_3$ PZMs at domain walls. We discuss both clean and disordered systems. In clean systems this mechanism requires a certain degree of control of the interaction strength and range. In contrast, disorder can provide a more generic route: While short-ranged, edge-uncorrelated disorder % on the two edges suppresses the simultaneous pinning required for stable parafermion modes, when the disorder on the two edges is sufficiently correlated, as expected for smooth disorder potentials, the parameter regime hosting PZMs increases.

papers.title_en: Non-Coulomb $Q$-Cohomology and Quantum Lifting
papers.abstract_en: We study quantum lifting of classical BPS cohomology classes in four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory. Certain powers of the gaugino bilinear $\mathcal S=\text{Tr}(λ_+λ_-)$ in orthogonal theories provide non-Coulomb monotones: multi-graviton classes that vanish upon Cartan restriction. For $SO(7)$, we identify $\mathcal S^4$ as a superconformal descendant of a known lifted monotone class, explaining the latter's non-Coulomb character, and explicitly construct a fortuitous lifting partner for $\mathcal S^4$. This construction provides a strategy for finding analogous partners for higher powers at higher ranks. Our main result establishes restrictions on the quantum lifting of classical BPS cohomologies for general gauge groups. We show that the one-loop correction $Q_1$ to the supercharge annihilates every monotone class in classical cohomology, while every non-zero $Q_1$ image is of non-Coulomb type. Thus every non-zero one-loop pairing has a fortuitous source and a non-Coulomb target, so that Coulomb monotones survive at this order at finite rank. In the BMN sector, our results imply that non-Coulomb monotones survive at one loop order as well. A crucial step in the argument shows that every non-Coulomb class, fortuitous or monotone, is annihilated in classical cohomology by a sufficiently high power of a scalar discriminant, which we interpret as a partial no-hair property.

papers.title_en: Stratification of opers with apparent singularities and isomonodromic bubbling
papers.abstract_en: On a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, we study Simpson's stratification of the de Rham moduli space of rank-2 flat connections. Upon representing flat $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-connections by branched projective structures, or equivalently by opers with apparent singularities, the stratum containing a flat connection is determined by the minimal number of apparent singularities needed to represent it. We construct explicit holomorphic families in which two simple apparent singularities collide and disappear, so that the family crosses into a smaller stratum; this realizes Simpson's closure relation between strata near generic points. The analogous families of Higgs bundles are described by Baker--Akhiezer divisors on the spectral curve in which two points converge to a pair of points exchanged by the spectral involution. We show that, before the collision, the two apparent singularities are joined by twin paths bounding a bubble, so that these families arise from the isomonodromic bubbling surgery discussed by Calsamiglia, Deroin and Francaviglia.

papers.title_en: Protected domains and cooperative invasion on weighted networks
papers.abstract_en: Reciprocal contacts can favor cooperation by protecting a lineage until its descendants compete as a group. An individual is chosen to reproduce from the whole population, with a probability increasing with its averaged cooperation payoff. Its offspring replaces a neighbor through contacts weighted equally in both directions. We compare a single cooperator taking over defectors with the reverse invasion, using the same distribution of introduction sites. When payoffs weakly affect reproduction, every network with at least six sites and a path visiting them all admits weights favoring cooperation at any benefit-cost ratio $b/c>1$. This holds for mutants placed uniformly or arising in newborn offspring. Unequal contacts sustain aligned domains around two protected sites, converting individual reproduction into collective competition. Cooperation cannot have an advantage when its benefit does not exceed its cost, at any positive selection strength with positive reproduction rates. Where mutants arise changes which contact patterns can use this mechanism. On a five-site path, the weak-selection threshold has the sharp lower bound seven under uniform placement; newborn introduction never favors cooperation at this order. We classify the contact patterns with at most five sites that can favor cooperation under either rule; newborn introduction requires a four- or five-site cycle. Tracing copies backward to their ancestors separates domain competition from the probability of reaching it. Exact polynomial inequalities prove sharp threshold bounds for paths and the four- and five-site cycles. The same ancestry reconstructs evolution without selection on weighted paths and cycles and fixes the slowest relaxation rate on every connected reciprocal network. Cooperation thus depends on both the collective competitors created by contacts and the route by which a new lineage enters them.

papers.title_en: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moiré Hubbard bands
papers.abstract_en: Moiré semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to 100mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. These observations distinguish the state from the reported strange metals associated with quantum criticality and favor the viewpoint that it is an intrinsic state of matter. We also report the observation of a new superconducting dome being developed from the ESM but far away from both the Mott insulating state and the van Hove singularity of the material. Our work opens the door to exploring the new regime of partially filled Hubbard bands in the clean limit.

papers.title_en: A binary black hole merger rate comparison within the same metallicity-star formation rate framework
papers.abstract_en: Recent studies have suggested that binary population synthesis models, when coupled with observationally based, metallicity-dependent SFRD, overpredict the observed local BBH merger rate density. The significance of this tension might vary depending on the specific code and parameters adopted. Thus, a more extensive exploration of the parameter space is required. Here, we perform such an extended analysis. We first carry out a comprehensive analysis by using a large set of BBH merger efficiencies across a wide range of physical assumptions, parameters, and initial conditions. We combine these efficiencies with an observationally motivated SFRD and explore 18 metallicity variations to encompass observational uncertainties. We find that the tension between predicted and observed BBH merger rate density persists: in 17 out of 18 metallicity variations none of the models considered predicts a local BBH merger rate within or below the observed 90% credible interval. Even in the most favorable metallicity variation, only <10% of the models are consistent with the observational constraints. Then, we perform a full calculation, including a self-consistent delay time distribution, for the models yielding the lowest BBH merger rate densities. This analysis confirms that even the most conservative models overpredict the observed local BBH merger rate for almost all the metallicity variations. We show that the inclusion of the low-metallicity tail contributed by low-mass galaxies and starbursts, together with a treatment of iron rather than oxygen abundance, systematically shift the predicted rates toward higher values. Consequently, even literature models that predict moderate BBH merger rates can instead produce substantially higher rates when coupled to an observationally motivated SFRD.

papers.title_en: Non-equilibrium dynamics of long-range field configurations in the Proca theory and the counterexample to the law of periodic charge oscillations
papers.abstract_en: Long-range field configurations exist in the Proca theory and their non-equilibrium evolution is of interest in this work. General arguments suggest that a charge can be assigned to them and that its evolution is governed by the law of periodic charge oscillations. We discuss an elegant analytically-solvable example of a field configuration in the Proca theory respecting such a law. We also identify a weak point in the aforementioned general arguments, construct the counterexample to the law of periodic charge oscillations in the Proca theory, and comprehensively discuss it. The Gibbs-Wilbraham phenomenon is discussed in the course of these studies.

papers.title_en: Exact algebraic separation of the gravitoelectromagnetic perturbations of Kerr-Newman-(anti-)de Sitter black holes
papers.abstract_en: We obtain an explicit separation of the coupled gravitational and electromagnetic radiative equations on nonextremal Kerr--Newman--(anti-)de Sitter black holes with nonzero charge and rotation. The construction uses a matrix with constant determinant, chosen independently of the frequency and azimuthal number, and treats the positive- and negative-spin sectors within the same formulation. We establish that this transformation is smooth and invertible throughout the open AdS exterior and between the event and cosmological horizons in dS. The resulting radial and angular systems are valid at arbitrary complex frequencies. We also express regularity of the radiative Newman--Penrose variables at the rotation axes and future horizons as conditions on the separated solutions. In the asymptotically flat limit, the transformation is related to Hintz's matrix integrating factor by the allowed frame freedom. These results provide a basis for studying quasinormal modes and black-hole stability in Kerr--Newman--(anti-)de Sitter spacetimes, as well as exploring holographic applications to strongly coupled systems.

papers.title_en: Dark Matter Axions Modulate Dark State Scintillation
papers.abstract_en: The decay rate of the thallium-iodine dark state in the popular alkali-halide scintillator NaI(Tl) modulates in phase with the dipole anisotropy of the cosmic microwave background (CMB), it is argued. Axion dark matter particles --- at rest in the local CMB rest-frame --- couple to the static magnetic field created in their rest-frame by the static electric quadrupole field within the tetragonally-distorted thallium-iodine octahedron surrounding each dark state. For axions with rest-mass energy near the roughly 0.5 eV dark state activation energy in NaI(Tl), the resulting near-infrared electric field created by this axion electrodynamic interaction modulates the dark state scintillation lifetime by bringing home the excited hole --- from the four in-plane iodine 5p orbitals that share it --- to the Tl 6s shell where it can recombine with the excited Tl 6p electron to produce the scintillation light.

papers.title_en: On connection between associators and 6j-symbols
papers.abstract_en: We propose a new formula relating the rationalized Drinfeld associators obtained from the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equation to the quantum $6j$-symbols of the algebra $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g})$: $ U_{q} = U \cdot Φ^{KZ}_{\mathbb{Q}} $. We prove this relation in the case of the $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ Lie algebra for the tensor cube of the fundamental and the first symmetric representation. We also check it perturbatively for the $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ algebra for representations $[2]\otimes [1] \otimes [1]$, $[2]\otimes [2] \otimes [1]$, the non-trivial cases with multiplicities --- $[2,1]^{\otimes 3}$, $[2,2]^{\otimes 3}$, and in the case of the $\mathfrak{so}_5$ Lie algebra for the tensor cube of the fundamental representation.

papers.title_en: Low temperature thermodynamics of $S_{\mathrm{eff}}=1/2$ triangular lattice quantum spin liquid candidate TlYbS$_2$
papers.abstract_en: Geometrically frustrated triangular-lattice antiferromagnets exhibit a delicate competition between magnetic order and quantum spin liquid (QSL) behavior, with the Yb-based delafossite family $A$Yb$X_2$ providing a structurally clean platform for exploring this physics. Here, we report a comprehensive study of single-crystal TlYbS$_2$ using DC magnetization, AC susceptibility, electron spin resonance (ESR), and specific heat measurements extending from room temperature to the millikelvin regime. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms a trigonal $R\bar{3}m$ structure comprising well-separated triangular layers of Yb$^{3+}$ ions with no detectable site disorder. At zero field, a weak thermodynamic anomaly is observed near $530$ mK, which may indicate the onset of a weakly ordered state similar to that reported in KYbSe$_2$. Below $300$ mK, the zero-field magnetic specific heat follows $C_{\rm m}\propto T^{1.8}$, close to a quadratic temperature dependence, in contrast to the linear temperature dependence reported for the sister compound TlYbSe$_2$, which has been described in terms of the interplay between spinons and thermally excited gauge-flux excitations. Magnetization and ESR measurements establish pronounced easy-plane magnetic anisotropy, with $g_\perp/g_\parallel \approx 6.9$. The anomaly near $530$ mK exhibits a strongly anisotropic response to magnetic field. For $H\perp c$, it remains visible up to approximately $2$ T and continuously evolves toward a field-induced ordered phase above approximately $2.5$ T, followed by a sequence of field-induced phases that includes a $1/3$ magnetization plateau between approximately $5$ and $8$ T and full polarization near $17$ T. In contrast, for $H\parallel c$, the anomaly weakens and is suppressed near $3$ T, consistent with the recently reported confinement--deconfinement transition from an ordered state to a field-induced QSL.

papers.title_en: Local wave-packet spectroscopy of the Drude weight in Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids
papers.abstract_en: We investigate wave packets generated by a local pulse electric field in a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) with a U(1) charge $q$. Bosonization shows that a local pulse field creates two counterpropagating packets with opposite accumulated charges $\pm qK$ and velocity $v$, where $K$ and $v$ are the TLL parameter and velocity. The packet motion produces a linearly growing charge polarization $P(t)=2 qDt$ in the conducting TLL at non-equilibrium, allowing the Drude weight $D=vK$ to be extracted from real-time local dynamics. We test this local-packet description by time-dependent variational principle simulations of the spin-1/2 XXZ chain. The simulations visualize the density, current, energy, and entanglement profiles in the space-time plane and confirm the predicted packet charge and propagation velocity. We also show that excess energy and entanglement remaining near the pulse region are suppressed in the weak-pulse limit. Finally, the Drude weight obtained from the packet-induced polarization agrees with the exact Bethe-ansatz result, demonstrating local-packet spectroscopy of intrinsic transport in a TLL.

papers.title_en: Einstein-Cartan and Palatini-Cartan Gravity from Graded Poisson Geometry
papers.abstract_en: Using notions from graded Poisson geometry, we develop a framework that allows for concise formulations of field theories such as Einstein-Cartan and Palatini-Cartan gravity. We show that Einstein-Cartan gravity is equivalent to a variant of Palatini-Cartan gravity in which the vielbein fields are constrained to satisfy appropriate symmetry relations, which we refer to as constrained vielbein gravity. To that end, we relate these theories via a diffeomorphism of graded manifolds. We then show how to obtain the full Palatini-Cartan theory by removing the symmetry constraint. Finally, we show how our graded geometric framework allows for a direct incorporation of the minimal BV extension of the graded constrained vielbein and Palatini-Cartan theories.

papers.title_en: Pt-induced semimetallic transport and enhanced thermoelectric response in the half-Heusler alloy YNi_{0.5}Pt_{0.5}Bi
papers.abstract_en: Half-Heusler alloys provide a versatile platform for tuning electronic and thermal transport through chemical substitution. Here, we investigate the thermoelectric and magnetotransport properties of spark-plasma-sintered YNi_{0.5}Pt_{0.5}Bi. Partial substitution of Ni by Pt drives YNiBi toward semimetallic transport, characterized by hole-dominated conduction, a low Hall carrier concentration of $\mathrm{1.9 \times 10^{19} cm^{-3}}$, and a sizeable nonsaturating magnetoresistance of 18$\%$ at 300 K under 14 T. Compared with YNiBi, Pt alloying increases the room-temperature Seebeck coefficient from approximately 90 to 130 $\mathrm{μV K^{-1}}$, while reducing the thermal conductivity to 3.15 $\mathrm{W m^{-1} K^{-1}}$. Single-parabolic-band analysis indicates an enhanced carrier effective mass, resulting in a room-temperature power factor of 13.7 $\mathrm{μW cm^{-1} K^{-2}}$ and a figure of merit ($zT$= 0.13). First-principles calculations further show a Pt-induced closing of the electronic band gap and a low density of states near the Fermi level, consistent with the experimentally observed semimetal-like transport. These results demonstrate that Ni/Pt alloying provides an effective route for simultaneously tuning the electronic, magnetotransport, and thermoelectric properties of YNiBi-based half-Heusler compounds.

papers.title_en: High-frequency water megamasers as precision probes of black holes, galaxies and cosmology: A case for a next-generation sub-mm/mm interferometer
papers.abstract_en: Water megamasers in the circumnuclear disks of active galactic nuclei are among the most precise probes of supermassive black holes. VLBI imaging of 22 GHz disk masers has provided geometric distances to independently constrain $H_0$, accurate black hole mass measurements, and sub-parsec views of accretion disk geometry. ALMA has opened a new window into water maser transitions in the sub-mm/mm regime, which trace temperatures, densities and disk regions that are inaccessible at 22 GHz, and can be observed at higher spatial resolution and with less free-free absorption. However, current detections are limited to a few bright extragalactic masers in nearby galaxies. We present the case for a next-generation sub-mm/mm interferometer - ALMA2040 - that would open a new parameter space for maser studies. We show that a 10-fold increase in line sensitivity and three times longer baselines compared to ALMA would transform sub-mm maser studies from a few bright detections into a population-level probe, delivering black hole masses and geometric distances from sub-mm masers alone, independent of and complementary to 22 GHz measurements. Integrated into a VLBI array, ALMA2040 would resolve maser disks out to $>$160 Mpc, extend maser black hole masses into the largely untested intermediate-mass regime, reveal magnetic field structure in accretion disks through polarization studies, and test systematics in $H_0$ measurements.

papers.title_en: The hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric lattice QCD with twisted-mass fermions
papers.abstract_en: We present a lattice-QCD calculation of the leading-order hadronic-vacuum-polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in isospin-symmetric QCD. We employ the gauge configurations generated by the Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration (ETMC) with $N_f = 2 + 1 + 1$ flavors of Wilson-clover twisted-mass quarks at four lattice spacings and at values of the quark-mass parameters matching the definition of isospin-symmetric QCD given in the FLAG review 2024 and in the 2025 edition of the Muon $g-2$ Theory Initiative White Paper (WP25). After retuning the simulation parameters to precisely match these two definitions of isospin-symmetric QCD, and after carrying out an extrapolation to the continuum limit based on the data at lattice spacings $a \simeq 0.049, 0.057, 0.068$ and $0.079$~fm, and spatial lattice sizes up to $L \simeq 7.7$~fm, we obtain $a_μ^{\rm HVP, FLAG}(\rm{iso}) = (720.0 \pm 6.9) \times 10^{-10}$ and $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso}) = (714.8 \pm 7.4) \times 10^{-10}$. Our results, which have a relative uncertainty of about $1 \%$, agree well with the corresponding determinations by other lattice groups. After adding to our determination of $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso})$ the leading isospin-breaking corrections provided in the WP25, namely $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}({\rm IB}) = 0.1(3.4)\times 10^{-10}$, we obtain for the full HVP the value $a_μ^{\rm HVP}= (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$. This result translates into a Standard Model prediction for the muon anomalous magnetic moment that is fully consistent with the latest result by the Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment and strengthens the tension between lattice QCD and data-driven (pre-CMD3) dispersive determinations.

papers.title_en: $d$-wave superconductivity in quintuple-layer bulk superconductor La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$
papers.abstract_en: The recent realization of bulk superconductivity in the quintuple-layer nickelate La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ opens new opportunities to probe the pairing symmetry of the reduced Ruddlesden--Popper (RP) nickelate family. Using an effective five-layer Hubbard model and variational Monte Carlo calculations, we find that a spin-singlet $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave state is energetically favored, while extended-$s$-wave pairing is strongly suppressed. Based on the optimized superconducting state, we further calculate several experimentally accessible observables. The tunneling density of states exhibits a characteristic V-shaped low-energy spectrum, the superfluid density shows a linear low-temperature depletion, the Knight shift decreases below $T_c$, and the spin-lattice relaxation rate follows $1/T_1T\propto T^2$, together providing consistent signatures of a clean nodal superconductor. Extending the same framework to related reduced RP nickelates, we find a robust $d$-wave tendency in infinite-layer LaNiO$_{2}$, while trilayer La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{8}$ at its nominal filling lies close to the boundary between $d$-wave superconductivity and a non-superconducting state. These results establish bulk La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ as a promising platform for determining the pairing symmetry of nickelate superconductors and suggest a common $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave pairing tendency across the reduced RP nickelate family.

papers.title_en: Properties and limitations of linear models for mutual coupling in 21 cm arrays
papers.abstract_en: Mutual coupling between elements of low-frequency arrays is a leading systematic for 21 cm cosmology, leaking bright foregrounds into otherwise clean regions of the power spectrum. Many mitigation models describe coupling as a linear combination of uncoupled signals re-radiated from neighboring feeds, but data suggest additional mechanisms. Inspired by antenna scattering theory, we decompose coupling into an antenna mode, constructed from translated isolated responses and expected to be removable by linear combination models, and a structural mode, the remainder. Full-wave simulations of HERA-like feeds and dishes in a 37-element hexagonal array show that the antenna mode accounts for only about 1% of the beam perturbation power, suggesting limited scope for mitigation with linear models. Two effects nevertheless lead to substantially better suppression. First, correlating beams and weighting them by the sky changes the modes' relative importance: correcting the antenna mode can remove more than half of the coupling power in simulated visibilities. Second, relaxing the coefficient relationships imposed by re-radiation allows linear corrections to remove structural-mode coupling too. Beam-derived corrections can reduce coupling power by over an order of magnitude in our noiseless simulations of perfectly redundant arrays. Fitting directly to known isolated visibilities reduces residuals further on the fitted field, but this target is generally unavailable in observations. Practical correction therefore requires additional constraints to separate the unknown sky from coupling while preserving the cosmological signal. We introduce an extension of holographic back-projection to coupled beams, providing an intuitive picture of these perturbations in the aperture plane.

papers.title_en: Spin effects in the particle current of Bose-Einstein condensates in synthetic gauge fields
papers.abstract_en: Spin reveals the rotational features of a system independently of its state of motion. Hence, it is not a relativistic quantity, despite giving rise to effects that emerge naturally from relativistic equations only. Within a non-relativistic framework these effects are not inherently captured, and have to be added by resorting to symmetry principles or to the asymptotic limit of the corresponding relativistic framework. We report on one of these effects: the divergenceless spin term in the particle current density of spinor Bose-Einstein condensates. It could be observed in the setup of a synthetic Hall system made with non-relativistic pseudospin-1/2 bosonic particles. By tuning the interaction strength, the system can show how the spin term in the particle current is needed for the local matching of classical drift velocity in the ground state of the non-interacting system, whereas for increasing interparticle interactions the spin-to-orbital current ratio decreases. In either case, since the overall particle velocity changes with the spin term contribution, so does its circulation in a loop, which in turn has physical consequences for its relationship with the Aharonov-Bohm phase shift.

papers.title_en: Anomalous Thermal Conductivity Reversal Driven by a Fluctuating Charge Density Wave
papers.abstract_en: For more than a century, the lattice thermal conductivity of crystalline solids has been known to decrease with increasing temperature, as the phonons that carry heat scatter more strongly via Umklapp processes. Here we report a pronounced violation of this rule in the layered charge-density-wave (CDW) metal 2H-TaSe2. Its in-plane thermal conductivity is strongly nonmonotonic: it peaks sharply at the 122 K ordering transition, collapses to a deep minimum near 210 K, and then anomalously reverses, rising with temperature to at least 350 K. Such a high-temperature reversal, in which a crystal conducts heat more efficiently as it is heated, is rare in crystalline solids. Its thermal conductivity minimum lies deep in the disordered phase well above the ordering transition, unlike the weak, transition-centered anomalies of other charge-density-wave systems, pointing to heat conduction governed by fluctuating rather than established order. Combining inelastic X-ray scattering, selected-area electron diffraction, and synchrotron X-ray diffraction, we attribute the reversal to phonons scattering off persistent, fluctuating charge order that survives more than 150 K above the long-range transition, to at least 300 K. A phenomenological phonon-CDW scattering model, tied directly to the measured diffraction linewidth and intensity, quantitatively reproduces the entire nonmonotonic curve. We also reveal that the charge order melts not abruptly but through a fluctuation- and defect-driven, weak first-order process, leaving short-range correlations far above the transition. This work establishes fluctuating charge order as a sensitive control knob for thermal transport in quantum materials and thermal conductivity as a powerful probe of the hidden charge order.

papers.title_en: X-ray point sources towards the giant radio lobes of Centaurus A
papers.abstract_en: Centaurus A (NGC 5128) is the nearest radio galaxy (d = 3.8 Mpc), so individual X-ray point sources can be resolved against its giant radio lobes. We test whether a compact X-ray source population over the lobes exceeds the expected field population, once the selection function, foreground stars and the cosmic X-ray background (CXB) are accounted for. From five Chandra/ACIS-I lobe pointings we build a 0.5-7 keV catalogue of 185 sources, with Bayesian hardness ratios, Gaia DR3 and AllWISE counterparts, and spectral fits to the eight brightest. The hardness-ratio distribution (median -0.17; 80% of sources below N_H = 10^22 cm^-2) is that of background AGN plus a few foreground stars. Above the flux at which half the footprint is covered, the good sample holds 83 sources, 9 of them foreground stars, against 101 expected background sources: 27% below the expectation (-1.5 sigma including a 15% normalisation uncertainty), with no excess. The 90% upper limit on a lobe-associated excess above 6.9x10^36 erg/s is N_lobe < 18, or < 38 for a conservative 30% normalisation uncertainty. With the usual resolved-source masking and CXB subtraction, no additional lobe-associated correction to diffuse-emission or inverse-Compton measurements is indicated.

papers.title_en: Repulsive ultralight dark matter from Hosotani mechanism
papers.abstract_en: We build an ultralight dark matter model with repulsive self-interactions, starting from a 5D action that only includes a $U(1)$ gauge field and several massive and charged free fermions. The dark matter scalar field corresponds to the fifth component of the gauge field, after compactification to 4D. Although the single-fermion case only leads to attractive self-interactions, two fermions can already give rise to repulsive self-interactions, thanks to a Scherk-Schwarz twist around the fifth dimension. We check the observational and theoretical self-consistency of this scenario, from the inflation stage to the current time. We find that large ranges of model parameters are allowed. For scalar masses below $10^{-12}$ eV the self-interactions are negligible and the model behaves as fuzzy dark matter. For higher masses the repulsive self-interactions govern the formation of solitons of astrophysical size. Larger sizes require a large initial misalignment or small masses in the fuzzy dark matter regime.

papers.title_en: A rigid commensurate host and a defect that switches: vacancies in the frustrated alternating spin-(1, 1/2) Heisenberg chain
papers.abstract_en: The alternating spin-$(1,\tfrac12)$ Heisenberg chain with a frustrating next-nearest-neighbor coupling $J_2$ loses its Lieb--Mattis moment through a discontinuous transition to a singlet whose nature was left open. Using an SU(2)-symmetric density-matrix renormalization group, in which the total spin is a quantum-number label, we identify that phase and follow a single vacancy through it. The total spin collapses directly from $S=L/4$ to $S=0$, with no partially polarized window. The singlet phase is critical: its singlet--triplet gap closes as $1/L$, its entanglement entropy grows logarithmically with a central charge $c\simeq1.8$, and its modulation wavevector, extrapolated from $L=80$ to $200$, is commensurate at $3π/4$ and independent of $J_2$ to $5\times10^{-5}$. Removing the central $S=1$ site switches the ground state of the doped chain from a triplet to a singlet at $J_2^{\ast}=0.3068(3)$, where the host shows no feature; the triplet is not bound to the vacancy but spread over one of the two segments it leaves. The transmission of correlations through the vacancy saturates at a finite value below $J_2^{\ast}$, $T(\infty)=0.102(15)$ and $0.036(9)$ at $J_2=0.28$ and $0.30$, and the cut-chain law $T\propto L^{-1}$ is excluded on both sides. We also show that the longitudinal correlator is not an observable in a triplet sector.

papers.title_en: Berry-Curvature Effect in Anomalous Transport
papers.abstract_en: A theory of the Berry-phase effect in anomalous transport in ferromagnets driven by statistical forces such as the gradient of temperature or chemical potential has been developed by Di Xiao et al in Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 026603 (2006) based on a field-dependent density of states generating an additional contribution to the current density. We present an alternative derivation of the Berry- phase effect in anomalous transport in altermagnets and noncentrosymmertric metals based on quasiclassic matrix kinetic equation. Along with anomalous Hall effect an anomalous heat flow and anomalous thermalelectric currents are derived.

papers.title_en: Putting a Temperature on Electron Correlation
papers.abstract_en: It is common wisdom that a better understanding of how to quantify electron correlation should lead to more efficient treatments of the correlation problem. Here, we not only substantiate this view but turn it into a concrete, systematic framework for ground states. Since prominent correlation measures such as the nonfreeness depend only on the one-particle reduced density matrix, modeling the correlation energy as a function of such a measure naturally places the framework within reduced density matrix functional theory, while keeping the cost at mean-field level. Strikingly, the variable conjugate to the measure emerges as a ``correlation temperature'', thereby connecting correlation measures, functional theory, and effective temperatures. The framework rationalizes methods such as i-DMFT, and we illustrate its key concepts analytically for the Hubbard dimer and numerically for small molecular systems. This brings a fundamental question within reach: how much of the correlation problem can be solved at mean-field cost?

papers.title_en: The gravitational constant and the cosmic microwave background
papers.abstract_en: The CMB constrains the gravitational constant $G$ at recombination to a few percent of its laboratory value, but the effect of $G$ on recombination itself is usually absorbed into a global fit rather than made explicit. We return to the semi-analytic description of the acoustic spectrum to ask how the acoustic scale $\ell_A$, the equality scale $\ell_{\rm eq}$ and the damping scale $\ell_{\rm damp}$ respond to a variation of $G$ during recombination, and where $G$ enters the residual ionization of the dark ages. We use a modified version of CLASS in which $G$ is varied through $λ_G \equiv \sqrt{G/G_{\rm N}}$, scanning $λ_G \in [0.25,2]$ at fixed physical densities and CMB temperature, with helium recomputed for each model. Analytic rate arguments are confronted with the numerical ionization histories, the visibility function, the Hu & White damping integral and the TT spectra. While $\ell_{\rm eq}$ and $\ell_A$ are nearly independent of $G$, non-equilibrium recombination gives $\ell_{\rm damp} \propto λ_G^{-0.304}$. The dependence exists only above a critical value of $G$, set by fundamental and cosmological parameters, a factor of 49 below $G_{\rm N}$. The dark-ages optical depth varies by only 16% for $G$ multiplied by 64, a negligible channel. Because $G$ enters only through the expansion rate, the imprint comes entirely from out-of-equilibrium recombination, and the competition between the atomic rates and the expansion is governed by one dimensionless combination, $α_G \equiv G m_e μ/\hbar c$, with $μ$ the mean mass of matter per photon. Each scale is the distance to last scattering divided by a length imprinted before it, so a late-time change of gravity rescales all three alike. The ratio $\ell_{\rm damp}/\ell_A$ therefore isolates $G$ at recombination and, up to lensing and screening, compares it directly with the laboratory value.

papers.title_en: Are $E>B$ regions essential for particle injection in relativistic magnetic reconnection?
papers.abstract_en: During relativistic magnetic reconnection, X-points ($E>B$ regions at vanishing guide field) have been proposed to play an essential role in injecting particles into the nonthermal population. Using fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations at a range of magnetizations $σ\equiv B_0^2/(4πn_0 m_e c^2) = 12$--$800$, we study in detail how the particle energy gains up to the injection threshold $γ_{\rm inj} = σ/4$ are partitioned into work done inside $E>B$ regions (unmagnetized), within one gyration after exit (re-magnetizing), and at all other times (magnetized). The magnetized channel supplies the largest part of the energy gain for $\sim 95\%$ of injected tracers at $σ= 12$ and $\sim 65\%$ at $σ= 800$. Most of the tracers in this magnetized majority never enter an $E>B$ region before injection. We also compare these injection shares with the earlier studies that proposed an essential role for $E>B$ regions. We conclude that $E>B$ regions are neither necessary for injection nor the dominant direct contributors to pre-injection work by injection share in two-dimensional, nonradiative pair-plasma reconnection at vanishing guide field.

papers.title_en: Superconducting properties of transition metal dichalcogenides in proximity to a conventional superconductor
papers.abstract_en: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) hold relevance for spin-triplet superconducting phases due to their inherent Ising spin-orbit coupling, but the majority of studies have so far focused on oversimplified models. In this work, we consider a TMD monolayer using a three-orbital model with anisotropic couplings and investigate the emergent superconducting properties when it is placed in proximity to a conventional spin-singlet $s$-wave superconductor. We find that the multiorbital nature of the TMDs lead to superconducting gaps not only at zero energy but also at higher energies, so-called hybridization gaps, which exhibit a complex structure due to the anisotropic couplings, challenging their spectral measurement. Moreover, we find that the inherent Ising spin-orbit coupling induces a spin splitting and a spin polarization along the $z$ direction, which correlates with the emergence of mixed spin-triplet superconducting pairs. These spin-triplet pair correlations appear in the monolayer as a proximity-induced effect due to the impact of the Ising spin-orbit field on conventional spin-singlet $s$-wave superconductivity. Taking realistic parameters for a $\text{MoS}_2$ monolayer, we show that the Ising field is strong enough to induce spin-triplet pair correlations of the same magnitude as their spin-singlet counterparts. We also include Rashba spin-orbit coupling, naturally emerging in a heterostructure and find that it induces equal spin-triplet superconducting pairs that compete with the mixed spin-triplet pairs induced by the Ising spin-orbit coupling. Our findings help understand the superconducting properties of TMDs in proximity to conventional superconductors.

papers.title_en: Inner Horizon Saddles and a Spectral KSW Criterion
papers.abstract_en: The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy formula $ρ= e^{A/4G}$ receives significant corrections for charged black holes near extremality. Using standard results in JT gravity, the correction term can semiclassically be expressed as minus the exponential of the inner horizon area, $e^{A_{\text{inner}}/4G}$, and the cancellation between these two exponentials enforces a vanishing density of states towards extremality, when the two horizons collide. Building on arXiv:2402.10162, we argue that the correction term corresponds to a complex saddle geometry of the bulk gravitational path integral. The proposed geometry has a negative boundary length and caps off at the inner horizon; we refer to it as the inner horizon saddle. We discuss how the saddle, and its accompanying minus sign, contribute to the density of states through a Picard-Lefschetz analysis of the inverse Laplace contour, together with a stability analysis of the saddle. We also address the inner horizon saddle's violation of the Kontsevich-Segal-Witten (KSW) allowability criterion for the inclusion of complex metrics. Despite this violation, which is believed to cause unphysical divergences in path integral computations, one can describe one-loop effects on the inner horizon saddle by carefully treating wrong-sign modes. Motivated by this observation, we propose a weaker version of the KSW criterion, which we call the spectral KSW criterion. Its purpose is to characterize when one-loop corrections around complex gravitational saddles are well defined.

papers.title_en: Axion String Source Modelling
papers.abstract_en: In this paper, we investigate the effect of the string radius of curvature $R_\mathrm{\,Gaussian}$ on the massive and massless scalar radiation emitted from collisions of travelling waves propagating along an axion (global cosmic) string. We construct initial conditions for two colliding Gaussians and perform parameter scans over their amplitude $A$ and standard deviation $σ_\mathrm{d}$. We show that these collisions emit isotropic bursts of massless radiation and that the energy emitted via this channel obeys a power law $\propto A^γ$, where the coefficient $γ$ depends on the regime of $A/δ$ and $δ$ is the string width. Massive radiation is exponentially suppressed $\propto e^{-ζR_\mathrm{\,Gaussian}}$ in the quasi-linear regime $σ_\mathrm{d} \gg δ$ and exhibits power-law decay $\propto R_\mathrm{\,Gaussian}^{-γ'}$ in the nonlinear regime $σ_\mathrm{d} \lesssim 2δ$, with different $ζ$ and $γ'$ in different regimes of $R_\mathrm{\,Gaussian}$. In this nonlinear regime, massive particle radiation can comprise up to 50\% of the total energy emitted. Drawing on a known parallel between axion radiation from global strings and gravitational radiation from Abelian-Higgs strings, this suggests that massive particle radiation may become significant with respect to the massless (gravitational) channel for such nonlinear burst signals. For all configurations studied, we obtain a spectral index $q \gtrsim 1$ for the axion radiation, where $q \rightarrow 1$ as $A$ increases, i.e. a higher proportion of radiation is emitted in high frequency modes.

papers.title_en: From Axion Detection to Dark Matter Astronomy
papers.abstract_en: A global haloscope network could turn an axion discovery into astronomy of dark matter substructure and transients. We combine interferometric phase, spatial coherence, and spectroscopy to study the formation and evolution of axion substructure through measurements of flow directions and velocity distributions. For tidal streams, a four-site forecast shows how longitudinal and transverse velocity dispersions can be measured jointly. Interpreted with dynamical and population models, these measurements could test axion production scenarios. Extensions to miniclusters, axion stars, and emitted bursts would broaden the astrophysical reach of laboratory detection.

papers.title_en: Aspects of Codimension two Holography in de Sitter Space
papers.abstract_en: Following \cite{Yadav:2024ray} we embark on a further study of the codimension two holography in de Sitter (dS) space. The $d$ dimensional bulk dS space is sliced by two end of the world $(d-1)$ dimensional branes which are bestowed with either Lorentzian dS or Euclidean AdS metric joining at a common $(d-2)$ dimensional space where the dual CFT lives. Through explicit computations of the holographic entanglement entropy, partition function, and Renyi entropy in both slicings for the bulk dS space emphasizing their similarities as well as differences we provide further evidence for this duality. We also make comments on further generalization of the codimension two holography.

papers.title_en: Operational Limits of Gravity-Mediated Entanglement
papers.abstract_en: Tests of gravity-mediated entanglement aim to determine whether two massive objects in spatial superposition can become entangled through their mutual gravitational interaction. In an ideal model, the two objects are often treated as pointlike branches, but real wave packets have a finite width and are also exposed to dephasing and residual non-gravitational forces. We study these effects in a two-branch gravitational cat-state model with Gaussian wave packets. The Newtonian interaction is averaged over the finite wave-packet width, and spatially correlated dephasing is included phenomenologically. We then ask a practical question: when does the generated state remain useful rather than merely entangled? To answer this, we examine Bell violation, teleportation fidelity, coherent information, Fisher information, and state distinguishability. We find finite parameter windows where the same state is Bell-nonlocal and teleportation-useful, but these windows shrink as the wave packets become broader or the dephasing becomes stronger. We also show that a residual electrostatic branch interaction can coherently cancel the gravitational nonlocal phase and strongly suppress the operational signal. The results identify finite-width and electrostatic tolerance boundaries that should be considered in future tests of gravity-mediated entanglement.

papers.title_en: The Radius-Luminosity Relationship for Active Galactic Nuclei with Hierarchical Bayesian Reverberation Mapping
papers.abstract_en: Reverberation mapping of active galactic nuclei uses the time taken for variability to travel through the system as a measure of system size, with this size being used to inform estimates of the mass of the central black hole, a technique that has graduated to an industrial-scale effort in recent decades. Such large target-count, multi-year surveys have been consistently undercut by poor light curve quality and the aliasing problems of seasonal observations. These impacts compound with statistical approaches that are not consistent between works and sometimes combine inconsistent statistical frameworks. Here, we present a new end-to-end Bayesian framework for fitting lags at scale in large surveys, simultaneous with the fitting of population models such as the radius-luminosity relation, and formulated in a numerically tractable way. This procedure is a statistically and numerically robust generalisation of the stacking and quality cut procedures of past works, fully marginalising over data uncertainty and data quality. Our approach remains numerically stable when scaling to larger surveys, and can act as a basis for any Bayesian population modelling of large sets of AGN time series observations. Applied to the OzDES sample, we demonstrate that this new approach yields more than double the constraining power on population-level properties like the R-L relationship, and an order-of-magnitude increase in the number of recovered lags and masses. With this method, we go from 24 high quality lag recoveries with traditional methods to a new effective sample size of ~297, all while being robust against random chance false positive measurements.

papers.title_en: Quantum models with the Yang-Lee phase transition
papers.abstract_en: In this article, we present four different $1+1$D quantum models that realize the Yang-Lee (YL) phase transition under a deformation that preserves $PT$ symmetry. These are the antiferromagnetic Ising spin chain in transverse and longitudinal magnetic fields, the massive Schwinger model, the Blume-Capel model, and the three-state quantum clock model. Using the state-operator correspondence, we identify the YL critical point, compute the scaling dimensions of the lowest operators in each model, and find perfect agreement with the exact results for the YL criticality in two dimensions. Using bosonization for the Schwinger model and the Polyakov-Hubbard transformation for the other models, we show that in all of these quantum models the YL critical point is described, as expected, by a massless bosonic field with an $i φ^3$ interaction. In the quantum clock model, this critical field interacts with a massive bosonic field, and we identify the massless and massive states in the Hamiltonian spectrum. In addition, we numerically compute the two-point function of $φ$ at the Yang-Lee critical point and show that it grows with distance, in agreement with theoretical expectations.

papers.title_en: Effective Field Theory for Holographic Compact Objects
papers.abstract_en: We study heavy-heavy-light-light correlators in holographic CFTs when the heavy operator is dual to a compact object localized on scales much smaller than the AdS radius. In the long-wavelength regime, the internal structure of the heavy state is described by a worldline effective field theory, whose local operators encode finite-size response coefficients such as tidal Love numbers. Focusing on weakly self-gravitating objects, we show that the Witten diagrams generated by local heavy-light interactions reorganize into the Born series of an effective wave equation for the light bulk field. We reproduce the same correlator by solving this wave equation with localized interactions and identify how the worldline Wilson coefficients are encoded in the CFT data. Our results provide a direct relation between the finite-size response of compact objects in AdS and the dimensions and OPE coefficients of heavy-light and light-light composite operators in the dual CFT.

papers.title_en: Monopole-deformed Kim-Park dualities from elementary dualities
papers.abstract_en: We derive the ellipsoid partition function identities for the monopole-deformed Kim-Park dualities of 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ adjoint SQCD with unitary gauge groups. The derivation uses only Aharony and Benini-Benvenuti-Pasquetti dualities as building blocks. By deconfining the adjoint into a $C_p[U(N)]$ quiver tail, we construct explicit duality sequences. Confinement and a rank-reducing duality chain then yield the expected magnetic partition functions, including the singlet contributions. We also present an alternative partition-function derivation of the $C_p[U(N)]$ s-confinement and provide Quiver Lab, a standalone HTML application for implementing and visualizing duality moves on quiver diagrams.

papers.title_en: Critical quench dynamics of Wegner's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge model: a geometric perspective
papers.abstract_en: Wegner's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge model is the earliest formulation of pure lattice gauge theory and predicts the topological nature of the confinement-deconfinement transition. In three dimensions ($D=3$), the equilibrium critical behavior of the model is understood in terms of geometrically defined objects, namely loop excitations and Fortuin-Kasteleyn (FK) clusters. This work investigates the critical quench dynamics of this model from a geometric perspective, following quenches from both a high-temperature percolation phase and the zero-temperature ground state. Using time-dependent finite-size scaling analysis, we find that the critical non-equilibrium relaxation of the percolation order parameter is governed by a dynamical exponent $z_{\rm p} \simeq 2.6$, consistent with that associated with the energy density, $z_{\rm c}$. Importantly, the value of $z_{\rm p}$ is robust with respect to the initial quench condition and the choice of geometrical objects. Furthermore, we provide a detailed characterization of the kinetics of different geometrical objects during the evolution from the percolation phase. Notably, we observe that the quench dynamics obeys dynamic scaling in terms of a growing lengthscale, $ξ_{\rm p}(t) \sim t^{1/z_{\rm p}}$, despite the absence of a local order parameter.

papers.title_en: On Algebraic Background-Independence
papers.abstract_en: It has recently been claimed that algebraic methods can be used to give a background-independent description of semiclassical gravity. This paper aims to provide an entry point into recent algebraic approaches to quantum gravity and to analyse and critically assess the conception of background-independence here involved. We discuss an algebraic framework for formulating an algebra of observables along the worldline of an observer in a cosmological setting. By 'gravitationally dressing' the observables to the observer's worldline, the reference to the spacetime background can be set aside at the level of the abstract *-algebra. Thus this *-algebra is taken to be independent of any particular spacetime realisation, with different states on the algebra corresponding to different backgrounds. We compare this algebraic framework to three influential notions of background-independence in the literature and argue that none of these fully captures the sense in which the *-algebra is taken to be background-independent. Building on this, we extract a novel notion of algebraic background-independence tied to the representation-independence of the *-algebra. This algebraic conception motivates two further concepts of background-independence tailored to semiclassical theories: semiclassical background-independence and perturbative background-independence. We suggest that these provide useful tools for evaluating the scope and limitations of semiclassical approaches to quantum gravity.

papers.title_en: Exciton superfluidity in two-dimensional bilayers at zero and high magnetic fields
papers.abstract_en: We study interlayer exciton superfluidity versus layer separation in two-dimensional electron-hole bilayers at zero magnetic field and quantum Hall bilayers at total filling $ν_T=1$. Unscreened Hartree-Fock theory predicts coherence at every finite separation, with an energy scale decaying inversely with separation at large distances. We examine how screening, correlations, and spatial instabilities modify this prediction. At zero field, we solve the linearized gap equation with the full momentum and frequency dependence of the interaction screened within the random-phase approximation, without an imposed cutoff. The apparent plasmon enhancement of pairing in the ladder approximation is largely cancelled by the second-order crossed-rung correction. Static screening determines the leading pairing exponent in the controlled high-density limit at fixed separation. At large separation, the pairing scale falls exponentially with squared separation while the instability persists. Extending this result to fixed density assumes Fermi-liquid layers and higher-order dynamical corrections subleading to the static pairing interaction. At high field, we obtain an analytic uniform Hartree-Fock saddle point in the lowest Landau level, coherent at every finite separation. Within Hartree-Fock theory, its finite-wave-vector collective-mode instability favors an excitonic supersolid, distinguishing loss of spatial uniformity from loss of coherence. We conjecture that the quantum Hall bilayer evolves continuously toward weak pairing of composite fermions, with a scale far below the mean-field prediction at large separation. This suppression could produce an apparent critical separation at finite temperature without a ground-state quantum phase transition. The comparison separates the existence, energy scale, and spatial stability of interlayer coherence.

papers.title_en: The impact of gamma-ray propagation effects on indirect dark matter searches
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we investigate dark matter (DM) detection in the context of weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs). Upon annihilation, WIMPs generate cascades of secondary particles through various channels, many of which culminate in the production of gamma rays. As these gamma rays travel toward Earth, their spectra are reshaped by interactions with the intervening medium. While current models typically account for attenuation via pair production on the extragalactic background light, they often neglect the fate of the resulting electrons and positrons, specifically subsequent inverse Compton scattering of these secondary particles, which can regenerate high-energy gamma rays. Here, we revisit the predicted gamma-ray fluxes from WIMP annihilation by performing a more detailed treatment of propagation effects. We show that for distant sources and annihilation channels such as $τ^+τ^-$, the full treatments can significantly alter the observed gamma-ray flux, by up to a factor of three orders of magnitude for heavy WIMPs. This has an impact on current dark matter limits derived without taking into account propagation effects, depending on the considered WIMP mass and annihilation channel. Our study demonstrates the importance of a detailed propagation treatment for indirect dark matter searches, and the need to account for such effects in order to obtain accurate, more reliable dark matter signal predictions and exclusion limits.

papers.title_en: Gravitational light deflection and shadows in a warm plasma
papers.abstract_en: Analytical studies of light bending in a dispersive medium near compact objects, e.g., black holes or neutron stars, are most challenged by a suitable definition of the medium. The most realistic model would be a hot magnetized plasma. In such a medium, however, an analytical description of light rays is very difficult. Therefore, usually an isotropic dispersive medium is assumed in analytical calculations. While it is possible to formulate equations for a general refractive index, which some studies do, most attention in the literature is given to the particular case of a cold, non-magnetized electron-ion plasma. Whereas this model covers many astrophysically relevant situations, there are indications that in some cases the plasma temperature is so high that the approximation of a cold plasma is no longer valid. For this reason, we consider in this paper a warm, non-magnetized electron-ion plasma, where the temperature is not set equal to zero but assumed to be small enough, such that relevant equations can be linearized with respect to it. After discussing the general equations for light rays in such a medium on a general-relativistic spacetime, we specify to the axially symmetric and stationary case which includes the spherically symmetric and static case. In particular, we calculate the influence of a warm plasma on the bending angle. In the spherically symmetric and static case, we also calculate the shadow in a warm plasma. We illustrate the general results with a static (respectively corotating) and an infalling warm plasma on Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes.

papers.title_en: Modified hydrogen recombination rate due to non-Hubble redshift effects
papers.abstract_en: The accumulation of observational data in recent years has led to a peculiar situation in which measurements of the cosmological parameters made by various collaborations and using different methods yield significantly different values. A solution to this problem may be found by modifying the models used to obtain these values. In this work, we revisit the standard approach to the recombination calculation and investigate a mechanism that can introduce corrections to the rate at which Lyman-alpha photons escape the resonance line. We find that interactions of Lyman-alpha line photons with moving neutral hydrogen atoms can become a source of such a correction. An analysis of CMB data for the modified model favors the existence of a non-Hubble redshift effect and prefers slightly higher values of $H_0$ and smaller values of $Ω_m$ and $S_8$ compared to the standard $Λ$CDM model, as well as a smaller value of the scalar spectrum index $n_s$.

papers.title_en: Symmetry and Quantum Geometry in Bloch Bands
papers.abstract_en: Quantum geometric quantities have featured heavily in the discussion of the properties of quantum systems in recent years. Among quantities most commonly discussed is the variance of Berry curvature and the integral of the trace of the quantum metric tensor. Despite their usefulness, it is known that they suffer from one significant complication: for a tight-binding model, the quantum geometric quantities depend not only on the parameters of the tight-binding model itself, but also the real space geometry of the tight-binding model, the so-called "orbital embedding". One explicitly geometry-independent quantity is therefore the minimal value of the quantum geometric quantity out of all possible real space geometries. In this work, we demonstrate that, if the tight-binding model is compatible with certain spatial symmetries, then the real space geometry that minimizes the variance of the Berry curvature or the integral of the trace of the quantum metric tensor must obey all those spatial symmetries. We further show that the statement is applicable to systems with magnetic translation symmetries and other composite symmetries, with implications for the quantum geometry of the Hofstadter model.

papers.title_en: Constraining Dark Acoustic Oscillations with the High-Redshift UV Luminosity Function
papers.abstract_en: Dark acoustic oscillations (DAOs) in the matter power spectrum can arise in many different dark sector models, and can imprint on a variety of cosmological observables. In this work we use measurements of the galactic UV luminosity function (UVLF) at high redshifts to constrain the dark acoustic oscillation feature at small scales in a model-agnostic way. We introduce a phenomenological transfer function model for a dark sector with a species undergoing DAOs which can accommodate sub-dominant dark matter abundances, and obtain constraints on its parameters. In order to predict the UVLF, we employ an Extended Press-Schechter formalism which we calibrate using N-body simulations with initial conditions featuring DAOs. Using measurements from the Hubble Space Telescope, James Webb Space Telescope, Subaru Telescope, and Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope, we constrain the wave number of the first DAO peak to be at $k \gtrsim 50\ h/\mathrm{Mpc}$, unless the fraction of dark matter undergoing DAOs is less than $0.07$.

papers.title_en: Breakdown of hydrodynamic universality in causal first-order viscous neutron star oscillations
papers.abstract_en: Hydrodynamic modeling of viscous neutron stars requires a choice of theory of relativistic hydrodynamics. That distinct formulations contain the same physical content in the long-wavelength limit is referred to as ``hydrodynamic universality.'' It has been recently shown that hydrodynamic universality can break down in radial neutron star oscillations: causality and finite-size effects restrict access to the long-wavelength universal hydrodynamic regime in sufficiently viscous stars. We show that this breakdown occurs for a broad range of causal hydrodynamic frames in Bemfica--Disconzi--Noronha--Kovtun (BDNK) theory. Increasing viscosity collectively pushes this class of causal frames away from the BDNK regime of validity, eventually forcing all to lie outside it at bulk viscosities in the range $ζ\sim10^{30}$--$10^{31}\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$. This breakdown of universality is accompanied by material changes in the oscillation mode structure: non-hydrodynamic modes become damped on timescales comparable to those of hydrodynamic modes, the first overtone can become longer lived than the fundamental mode, and unphysical instabilities with sub-millisecond timescales can emerge. Even in regimes where universality has broken down, we find that the inviscid threshold of gravitational collapse remains unchanged in BDNK theory. These results provide evidence that first-order theories of relativistic hydrodynamics may be insufficient for modeling sufficiently viscous neutron stars.

papers.title_en: Spin-1/2 Heisenberg diamond-like decorated honeycomb lattice in a magnetic field from the perspective of localized magnons and exact diagonalization
papers.abstract_en: The spin-$1/2$ quantum Heisenberg model on the diamond-decorated honeycomb lattice in a magnetic field is investigated using complementary analytical and numerical methods. The ground-state phase diagram comprises Lieb-Mattis ferrimagnetic, dimer-tetramer, monomer-dimer, spin-canted, and saturated paramagnetic phases, giving rise to characteristic magnetization plateaus, continuous and discontinuous field-induced transitions. In the highly frustrated regime, a localized-magnon approach based on an effective classical lattice-gas model provides an accurate description of the low-temperature magnetism and thermodynamics in agreement with numerical results. At intermediate frustration, finite-temperature calculations reveal characteristic specific-heat signatures of the field-induced transitions including the development of Ising critical behavior at the field-induced transition between the monomer-dimer and Lieb-Mattis ferrimagnetic phase.

papers.title_en: Stimulated capture of axion dark matter around primordial black holes
papers.abstract_en: We study the stimulated capture of axion and axion-like particles around primordial black holes, mediated by quartic self-interactions. We identify the parametric regions where Bose-enhanced growth overcomes cosmological dilution and derive analytic criteria for efficient formation and long-term survival of the hydrogenic ground-state cloud, confronting them with current bounds on axion-photon couplings. We discuss observational implications of these PBH+cloud systems, including resonant axion-to-photon conversion in neutron star magnetospheres and finite-size microlensing distortions. In the former case, the resonance condition selects a conversion shell outside the neutron star surface, and we show that the large axion occupation number of the cloud can compensate for the small conversion probability. The resulting transient line flux densities can exceed nominal VLA and ALMA sensitivities in regions where the Galactic encounter rate is observationally relevant. Independently, when the cloud size becomes comparable to or larger than the Einstein radius, finite-size effects can modify the standard point-lens microlensing light curve.

papers.title_en: Static electric and magnetic traversable wormholes in $(2+1)$-dimensional nonlinear electrodynamics
papers.abstract_en: Every traversable wormhole reported so far in static (2+1) gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics has come from a power-Maxwell Lagrangian L propto |F|^k restricted to k=1/2, always forcing the cosmological constant to a fixed sign or zero. We show these restrictions are artefacts of that single choice, not physical requirements, and give a complete classification of static traversable wormholes in this theory. Of the three mutually exclusive electromagnetic configurations compatible with the symmetry, the radial electric branch admits no throat for any Lagrangian or Lambda. In each remaining branch, azimuthal electric and magnetic, the field equations admit exactly two regimes: either the redshift function is fixed, leaving the shape function b(r) completely free with Lambda absorbed without constraint; or the redshift is generic, in which case b(r) becomes fixed instead. We solve both regimes in closed form in both branches, and show that fixing the Lagrangian to any single power k forces Lambda nonzero and determines b(r) up to finitely many constants: this freedom requires the Lagrangian to be genuinely unrestricted. One azimuthal-electric family reproduces the static BTZ mass function, turning the vacuum black hole into a wormhole once sourced by the nonlinear field. Applied to the unique conformal power-Maxwell theory, k=3/4, previously known only as a radial-branch charged black hole, the same Lagrangian yields genuine wormholes in the azimuthal and magnetic branches, showing the electromagnetic configuration, not the Lagrangian, decides between a horizon and a throat; Born-Infeld electrodynamics admits no throat in any branch.

papers.title_en: Radial Oscillations of Viscous Stars
papers.abstract_en: Oscillation modes of neutron stars, a key target for third-generation gravitational wave detectors, encode key information about their constituent nuclear matter. In this work, we study the effect of viscosity on oscillations of cold, polytropic, spherically symmetric neutron stars. We focus on purely radial oscillations and work perturbatively to linear order within two hydrodynamic frameworks: the acausal covariant generalization of the Navier-Stokes equations proposed by Eckart, and the causal generalization formulated by Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha, and Kovtun (BDNK). We find that viscosity damps the radial modes on millisecond timescales and induces fractional shifts in the oscillation frequency which increase both with the compactness and viscosity of the star, reaching up to the percent level for the fundamental mode with bulk viscosities $ζ\sim10^{30}\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$. For more viscous stars, the oscillation frequency decreases, becoming zero (i.e., an overdamped mode) for $ζ\gtrsim10^{31}\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$. We also study the linear threshold of gravitational collapse. Consistent with recent analytic results in the zero heat conductivity limit, we find that viscosity in Eckart theory cannot stabilize an unstable inviscid star. We provide numerical evidence that viscosity in BDNK theory is similarly unable to prevent gravitational collapse, but it slightly modifies the threshold of collapse. Overall, our results advance our understanding of the impact of viscosity on the oscillation modes of neutron stars, a key component of viscous asteroseismology with next-generation gravitational wave detectors.

papers.title_en: Beyond the BLUE I: the advantage ceiling - how much can any estimator beat the matched filter in mm/submm survey data?
papers.abstract_en: Papers claiming that convolutional neural networks outperform the matched filter are now common in astronomy. Since that filter is the best linear unbiased estimator (BLUE) for any noise of given covariance, and the minimum-variance unbiased estimator under Gaussian noise, such a claim requires that the noise covariance varies from image to image or the noise is non-Gaussian. We introduce the advantage ceiling eta >= 1, which quantifies both cases: the Fisher information for the amplitude in units of the matched filter's, computable from noise-only simulations before any network is trained, and a bound on the variance of any estimator unbiased at each true amplitude. We compute eta for a suite of millimeter/submillimeter survey noise models and for compact and extended source templates, using a variational score-matching ladder whose rungs are estimator classes of increasing statistical order, from linear to convolutional. With an instrumental white-noise floor, Gaussian noise returns eta = 0.94-1.06 (+-0.04); covariance mixtures give exact ceilings of 10.2 (spectral tilt, extended source), 2.1 (leaked components) and 1.1-1.8 otherwise; residual artifacts give eta <= 1.09. Source confusion gives the largest advantage, eta >= 3.8 (extended) and >= 2.4 (compact). Three unmodelled channels - a zeroed DC mode, a missing white floor and floating-point rounding - can manufacture spurious advantages of up to two orders of magnitude. A ResNet regressor is 6-15% less efficient than the matched filter on Gaussian noise once prior shrinkage is divided out, and realizes a factor 1.8 of the 10.2 available on the spectral-tilt mixture; a companion paper tests such regressors against these ceilings.

papers.title_en: Entanglement and apparent thermality in simulated black holes
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the apparent thermality of Hawking radiation in the semi-classical limit of quantum black holes using the mean-field limit of a chiral spin-chain simulator, which models fermions propagating on a black hole space-time in the continuum. In this free-theory regime, no genuine thermalisation occurs. Nevertheless, we show that a bipartition across the event horizon yields a reduced density matrix whose mode occupations follow an apparent thermal Fermi-Dirac distribution. In contrast, partitions away from the horizon do not exhibit such thermal distributions, reflecting the absence of thermal behaviour. Our results demonstrate that Hawking radiation appears thermal only with respect to horizon bipartitions in free theories, with genuine thermal behaviour expected to emerge only in the presence of strong interactions deep in the black hole interior, a study of which we leave for future work.

papers.title_en: Vortex clusters and vortex-filled bubbles in a modified Abelian-Higgs model
papers.abstract_en: We investigate a single-component Abelian-Higgs model with an eighth-order scalar potential whose vacuum manifold consists of two disconnected circles. The model supports two species of vortices and domain walls interpolating between the two vacuum components. We find type-1.5-like behavior characterized by nonmonotonic intervortex interactions and bound states of spatially separated vortices. Inner-vacuum vortices form clusters through short-range repulsion and long-range attraction, whereas outer-vacuum vortices form vortex-filled bubbles in which a closed domain wall confines multiple inner-vacuum-vortex cores. We construct the domain wall analytically, derive the asymptotic vortex-wall interactions, and analyze the fluctuation spectra of coincident multivortices to identify their splitting instabilities.

papers.title_en: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
papers.abstract_en: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.

papers.title_en: Finite $N$ black hole cohomologies
papers.abstract_en: We study new cohomologies for the BPS operators of the $\mathcal{N}=4$ Yang-Mills theory with $SU(3)$ and $SU(4)$ gauge groups, to better understand the black hole microstates. We first study the index of these black hole operators and identify their apparent threshold levels. For $SU(3)$, we find many towers of states and partial no-hair behaviors. We explicitly construct the threshold cohomology in the $SU(3)$ theory. We study throughout this paper a subsector of the field theory corresponding to the BMN matrix theory. We also argue that the BMN sector exhibits a black hole like entropy growth at large $N$.

papers.title_en: New Massless Spectra from Cosmic String Cusps
papers.abstract_en: In the standard picture of cosmic strings, cusps are generic features of Nambu-Goto loops where the string momentarily reaches the speed of light.
